summary: The schemas.v11 retarget, source-provenance split, declared successor roster, and corpus process-freeze verify. Acceptance still fails at 1 blocker and 3 SHOULD-FIX: the archive profile does not force one byte stream or reconcile its induced path limit; fixture coverage is not member-level; health evidence can disappear by omission; and the predecessor ledger erases two still-open advisories.

measurements.result: Subject matched dispatch at review start; predecessor and both frozen v3 verdicts matched their required digests. Duplicate-key-rejecting parses passed for v3 and v4.

All 14 recordedInputs/governingSources digests, both quoted-source pins, the predecessor pin, and both predecessor-verdict pins matched live bytes at initial measurement. Corpus v3 and schemas.v11 are mode 0444 at their recorded digests.

A recursive value diff found 56 changed leaves. Every changed leaf is at, or below, a path named by /basedOn/method's closed roster; no silent out-of-roster mutation was found. This check addresses delta honesty only and does not validate the changed values.

The live file-08 and COORD digests matched their pins. measuredRowStandingsAtFile08Digest is now faithful to the pinned register cells, while D-103/D-104 facts are separately attributed to the pinned COORD bytes. The subject remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, leaves DR-120 and DR-103 OPEN, and neither authorizes implementation nor chooses a packager, toolchain, or CLI.

The DR-120 row was exact and unique at its claimed source line. File 02 lines 86-121 and C-1..C-14 were exact. OBL-1..OBL-5 all have answeredAt entries; OC-1..OC-9, S-1..S-4, CI-1..CI-4, and AT-1..AT-7 are structurally present. Presence did not cure the substantive findings below.

schemas.v11 declares 45 requires strings across eight TC classes plus conditional arms. fixtureClassRides has eight TC keys, one free-form value per class; fixtureClassCoverage likewise keys only by class. Mixed producer/outcome/ride members therefore cannot be represented at FG-1's claimed member granularity.

Codex v3 actually records 2 blockers, 2 SHOULD-FIX, and 2 advisories. v4 faithfully lists the blocker and SHOULD-FIX IDs under qualified names but records advisories=[] and notFoldedThisSuccessor=[], omitting CPCV3-A1 and CPCV3-A2 while both underlying texts persist. Claude v3's 0/2/1 inventory is faithfully listed.

The profile was evaluated as a byte-producing algorithm, not merely searched for a format token. POSIX permits both preferred and alternate regular-file typeflags and permits application-selected physical blocking with undefined bytes after the two zero records; v4 chooses neither. Its permitted Unicode path strings also have no archive-byte encoding. Identical trees therefore do not force identical archive bytes.

blockers.title: The purported closed archive profile still permits different archive bytes for the same TreeCommitment and silently narrows the live schema's open path surface
detail: POSIX ustar names a family of conforming archives, not one byte-producing recipe. The profile never fixes the conversion of a permitted NFC Unicode tree-path string to header bytes, gives no exact file/dir/symlink typeflag mapping, and does not state the exact end-of-archive length or trailing-block contents. The cited POSIX format permits application-selected physical blocking and says blocks after the two zero blocks contain undefined data. Therefore two adapters can write different bytes, and different archiveDigest values, for the same ordered tree while satisfying every v4 sentence.

The bijection sentence constrains member count but does not normatively bind each regular-file body to the TreeCommitment length/sha256 or each symlink linkname to the target under a fixed byte encoding. It consequently is not a complete tree-to-archive serialization algorithm.

prefix='empty' plus refusal when a path does not fit the 100-byte ustar name field creates a packaging path-length limit; the equally 100-byte linkname field has no overflow rule for symlink targets at all. The consumed schemas.v11 deliberately leaves path length and oversized-input refusal OPEN in OD-1, while this subject's OD-P2 still says the schema caps are UNSPECIFIED and even points to historical schemas.v2. A schema-valid v11 tree can thus be rejected—or become unencodable—at a limit the subject simultaneously labels undecided.

archiveProfile.emittedAs also says CI-1 pins the profile token, but CI-1's exhaustive list names source tree, tool closure, adapter version, platform target, and exception approvals only. The profile ID is carried in OC-2 and the report, which is useful, but the claimed CI pin is absent.
blockers.externalStandardEvidence: ISO/IEC 9945-1:1990 / IEEE Std 1003.1-1990, Data Interchange Format, records the 100-byte name field and application-selected blocking with undefined data after the two zero blocks: https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-C13-bf1fc57a5dbcaa993cebad99aca83f64/pdf/GOVPUB-C13-bf1fc57a5dbcaa993cebad99aca83f64.pdf
blockers.impact: CI-3's same-input/same-archiveDigest promise is not testable across adapters, and the common boundary can reject live-schema-valid component trees without an owned, reviewed cap. This leaves the core CODEX-V3-B2 determinism defect materially open despite the new token and container name.
blockers.minimumRepair: Specify a complete, versioned tree-to-byte algorithm: exact pathname/link-target encoding, header field and typeflag bytes, file/symlink/directory body rules, numeric/checksum padding, data padding, exactly defined zero-block/trailing length, and byte-to-TreeCommitment validation. Reconcile the ustar name capacity with schemas.v11 OD-1 and this artifact's open-decision accounting rather than minting a hidden refusal. Actually pin archiveProfileId in CI-1 and add cross-implementation golden/negative cases for byte identity, member/body/target mismatch, extra members, and boundary-length paths. This remains tool-neutral and need not select a packager.

shouldFix.title: fixtureClassRides is a class-level list of alternatives, not FG-1's exact member-level coverage map
detail: schemas.v11 has 45 separate requires strings across eight TC classes, plus conditional arms. v4 supplies only eight TC-* map entries: one free-form string per top-level class. Those strings do not identify member ordinals/IDs, do not record per-member expected outcomes, and frequently say 'or', so they cannot establish FG-1's claim that every applicable member maps to exactly one producer with an expected outcome.

The mismatch is observable inside mixed classes. TC-ACCEPT's map says production S-3-EMIT even though its lock member is deferred on DR-111/ID-DEP-P2. TC-DUP mixes three refusal cases and two ACCEPT cases while its map offers alternative producers. TC-SIG has active refusal members plus canonical-preimage, ceremony, and future-lock arms on distinct dependencies; TC-BYTE-EXACT similarly mixes active cases with canonicalization and lock arms. The class-only report key permits only one standing and one ride for each such mixture.

The generic evidence requirement for standing=produced pins one class-level evidence object; it does not prove that all members were produced, nor can it reject a missing member or assign the specific lawful ride for one blocked arm. The claimed CODEX-V3-S2 repair is therefore not implemented, and part of the class-scoped-exemption claim is not representable.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Replace the free-form class strings with a normalized, closed member/arm map keyed to every schemas.v11 requirement and conditional arm. Give each entry exactly one producer/harness kind, exact ACCEPT or refusal expectation, evidence requirement, and—only when blocked or inapplicable—the one owning dependency. Make fixtureClassCoverage report those member keys and reject missing, duplicate, alternative, or class-wide stand-ins.

shouldFix.title: Health evidence is digest-bound only if voluntarily claimed, so required health applicability/result coverage can disappear silently
shouldFix.detail: OC-6 says the report records health-probe applicability, but the report shape has no applicability or standing field and requires {path, sha256} only 'when a health result is claimed'. AT-4 requires the opaque subprotocol tokens and no translation, but does not close that omission. A report with no healthResult can therefore satisfy the stated shape without distinguishing not-applicable, blocked, not-run, or missing evidence. The new evidence object repairs an unconstrained reference when present, not the completeness obligation in the DR-120 acceptance cell.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Add an explicit health standing/applicability record at the relevant role/platform scope; require {path, sha256} for every executed pass/fail result, and permit omission only through a closed, owner-specific not-applicable or blocked ride that report validation checks.

shouldFix.title: The predecessor ledger falsely erases two open Codex v3 advisories
detail: The frozen Codex v3 verdict contains CPCV3-A1 and CPCV3-A2, but v4 records codexV3.advisories as [], omits both from idCollisionNote and honestyRepairsFromV3, and declares notFoldedThisSuccessor empty. This is a source-recording error, not an interpretation difference.

Both underlying texts remain unchanged: reviewer guidance still says this is a first candidate and predecessor accounting is N/A, and CI-3 still requires identical report members while inputPins includes an opaque runId without saying whether it is deterministic or excluded from the reproducible tuple. The advisers remain advisory-grade individually, but representing them as nonexistent makes the successor ledger materially incomplete.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Record CPCV3-A1 and CPCV3-A2 with their actual standing and either carry them explicitly in notFoldedThisSuccessor or repair them: remove/historicalize the first-candidate instruction and define runId's relationship to CI-3 reproducibility. Do not claim an empty not-folded set while either text persists.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: Live-target attack: no operative emission/admission or corpus rule still targets schemas.v2; schemas.v11 is pinned and used.
Provenance-misattribution attack: file-08 cell measurements and adopted COORD facts are now distinct and digest-bound.
Bare produced-fixture-reference attack: fixtureClassCoverage does require {path, sha256} when standing=produced. CPCV4-S1 instead concerns missing member-level coverage and mixed rides.
Missing archive-profile identifier attack: archiveProfileId is present in OC-2 and conformanceReport.subject. CPCV4-B1 instead refutes the claimed byte closure and CI pin.
Silent corpus retarget attack: corpus v3 matches its recorded digest, is mode 0444, and the contract requires a new corpus version for a future retarget.
Silent successor-delta attack: every one of the 56 changed leaves falls within the declared v3-to-v4 roster.
Authority and implementation-reservation attack: no positive DR-120/DR-103 SATISFIED or QUALIFIED claim, implementation authorization, or concrete packager/toolchain/CLI choice was found.
verdictBasis: REJECT: 1 blocker and 3 SHOULD-FIX. The prompt permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: This independent review rejects component-packaging-contract.v4 at the measured subject digest. It does not mark DR-120 or DR-103 SATISFIED, does not apply or seal the subject, and does not authorize implementation. A successor can preserve the verified repairs while closing CPCV4-B1 and CPCV4-S1..S3.
coordinatorNote: Issue a successor rather than applying v4. Preserve the verified schemas.v11 retarget, source split, roster closure, and corpus freeze; replace the archive prose with a complete tree-to-byte profile, make fixture/report coverage member-addressable, make health omission governed, and restore truthful predecessor accounting.
